steps.body: A **ten frame** has 10 spots. Fill every spot to make **10**! Some empty? Find how many **more** make ten.

widget.prompt: 8 dots are here. Tap the empty spots to MAKE TEN.

commonCounts.feedback: So close — 9 fills only one spot. One more makes 10: 8 and 2.

widget.missFeedback: 8 is here. Fill the 2 empty spots: 8 and 2 make 10.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents make ten.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for make ten must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines make ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: Four more spots fill the frame: 6 and 4 make 10.

steps.body: Every number has a **ten partner**: 6 and 4, 9 and 1, and **5 and 5**. Each pair makes **10**.

3 needs 7 more to fill the ten frame.

3 and 5 make 8 — two spots left. 7 more make 10.

steps.body: You can MAKE TEN! Fill the empty spots to find the ten partner. Course complete!
takeaways: A ten frame is full at 10.
Every number has a ten partner: 6 and 4, 9 and 1, 5 and 5.
Find how many MORE make ten by filling the empty spots.
steps.teaser: That completes Counting & Numbers — see you in Shapes & Sorting!

concept.body: A ten frame is full at 10. Count the empty spots to find how many MORE make ten.

explanationVariants: Two more dots fill the frame: 8 and 2 make 10.
